claims.claim: Specificity is compared in ordered ID, class/attribute/pseudo-class, and type/pseudo-element columns.
A selector with an ID is more specific than a selector with no IDs regardless of its class and type counts.
Universal selectors and combinators do not add specificity.
`:is()`, `:not()`, and `:has()` take the specificity of their most specific argument, rather than adding their own pseudo-class weight.
`:where()` always has zero specificity, including the selectors in its argument.
Specificity is not the entire cascade; it is relevant when competing declarations are compared at the same origin and importance.
